code_findings.title: BrowserConfig accepts chrome_remote_debugging_port=None, and when the built-in browser setup path reaches its port-conflict check, it raises TypeError by passing None as the AF_INET port to socket.con
code_findings.explanation: The newly added field is annotated as int | None, so an explicit None is valid configuration. The built-in setup path then uses that value directly as the port in ('localhost', self.config.chrome_remote_debugging_port). An AF_INET socket address requires a concrete port; None therefore raises TypeError at connect_ex. The evidence does not establish the exact exception on the user-provided-browser path or whether None was intended to disable debugging versus select the default, so the supported claim is limited to the built-in path.
code_findings.impact: Caused by the change: This change introduces an explicitly nullable port configuration and makes browser setup consume that configured value. With chrome_remote_debugging_port=None, formatting the Chrome argument succeeds as '--remote-debugging-port=None', after which the built-in setup passes None to socket.connect_ex as the port and raises TypeError before launch.
